definition: In a polish/spline-adjustment pass, hip rotation is treated as the primary lever for correcting a pose's balance against an extending limb — when a leg reaches or kicks out in a direction, the hips are rotated to tweak toward that same direction — and hip balance is checked and fixed FIRST, before working outward through the chest, spine, neck, head, arms and legs.
purpose: Restore a pose's balance and readability after blocking and in-betweening are done, by correcting the one joint (the hips) whose rotation most directly compensates for an extending limb's effect on the body's overall balance.
visible_effect: The hips visibly rotate or shift toward the side a reaching or kicking limb extends, rather than staying square or rotating the opposite way, keeping the pose looking balanced rather than off-kilter.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A pose with correctly balanced hips reads as physically grounded and intentional; an uncorrected pose (hips left neutral while a limb reaches far from center) reads as tipping or unbalanced even if every other joint is posed correctly.
physical_interpretation: An approximation of how a real body keeps its centre of mass over its base of support: extending a limb shifts mass away from centre, and the hips (the body's own centre of mass region) compensate by rotating or shifting toward the extension.
use_cases: a polish pass on an already-blocked reference-driven animation (running, jumping, vaulting), checking hip rotation against each extending limb
any pose where a limb reaches, kicks, or extends noticeably far from the body's centerline
non_use_cases: a pose or style that deliberately wants an off-balance, falling, or unstable read — correcting hip balance would undo the intended effect
a limb motion small enough that it does not meaningfully shift the body's balance
interactions: Structural understanding — this is a concrete, actionable version of that card's balance concern, naming the SPECIFIC joint (hips) and the specific rule (rotate toward the extending limb) rather than balance in the abstract

Body lead — the same chain-depth-outward order this dimension already encodes for INITIATING motion (hips/root first) reappears here as the order for a REVIEW/polish pass: check and fix hip balance first, then chest, spine, neck, head, arms and legs outward from there

Physical reference timing method (W01 video 9) — this video's key-pose contact timing is taken directly from a real reference clip's exact frame numbers, a second independent confirmation of that technique, applied specifically to CONTACT points rather than the whole action's duration
cadence_representation: Directly checkable with a capability that did not exist when the `structural_understanding` card was written: `ai/pose.js measurePose` now computes a volume-proxy centre of mass and balance against a DECLARED support polygon (`balanceOf`) — exactly the measurement this hip-correction rule is informally approximating by eye. This is worth flagging plainly: the existing `structural_understanding` knowledge card still states "Cadence models neither" balance nor volume, and `appeal`'s card still claims no line-of-action measurement exists — both are now stale relative to `ai/pose.js`, which measures line of action, a centre-of-mass proxy, and balance against a declared support polygon at every authored key. A hip-rotation balance rule like this one could be checked directly against real `balanceOf` output rather than left to a human's eye, once support is declared.
control_surface: `ai/pose.js measurePose` (`centre_of_mass`, `balance`) already computes the needed measurement when `support` is declared; nothing currently applies a HIP-ROTATION CORRECTION based on a measured imbalance — the measurement exists, the corrective edit does not.
detection_and_measurement_methods: `ai/pose.js measurePose`'s `balanceOf` function reports whether the centre-of-mass proxy falls inside the convex hull of declared support effectors — a real, working measurement, though it requires the caller to declare which effectors are planted (MOT-016: nothing infers a contact automatically).
generation_or_modification_methods: None yet — no strategy in `ai/plan.js` adjusts hip rotation specifically in response to a measured balance shortfall; `authorMotion` can place a hip rotation value as part of an authored pose, but nothing derives that value FROM a balance measurement.
failure_modes: leaving the hips neutral or square while a limb reaches far from the body's centerline, producing a pose that reads as tipping regardless of how well the reaching limb itself is posed
correcting hip balance so strongly it reads as an exaggerated lean rather than a natural weight shift
roblox_considerations: None specific — a pure pose-balance concept independent of the target engine, directly applicable to any Roblox rig's hip/waist joint.
examples: a running-jump-vault sequence where, after blocking and in-betweening are complete, hip rotation is added specifically "according to the legs and body movements to have a better balance of the pose" — when the extending leg kicks out toward a direction, the hips are rotated toward the same direction (video @ 20:31–20:48)
the same polish pass then working outward from the hips through chest, spine, neck, head, arms and legs, in that stated order (video @ 21:01–21:15)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/7CBcvu8HLEQ @ 20:31–21:15 — stated directly in the transcript; a frame at t=20:41 in this session's sample directly confirms the corresponding stage on screen: a Maya viewport showing the rigged character mid-vault pose with the graph editor open on a hip/root controller's curves, alongside a small reference-video inset; experimental until validated
